name: Omali Yeshitela: 1966 City Hall mural custody

case.charges: 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural removal: destruction of city property and disorderly breach of the peace (municipal); grand larceny (state).
case.convicted: Municipal convictions; state conviction vacated in 1970, followed by reconviction upheld in 1972. Further U.S. Supreme Court review denied October 15, 1973.
case.sentence: Municipal sentence: 180 days in county jail. Initial state sentence: six months to five years, with 170 days credited. Anita Richway Cutting's 2000 USF thesis dates his initial release on $2,500 bond to March 29, 1968. After a separate Gainesville arrest and revocation of both bonds, he obtained release on May 29, 1968. At the November 13, 1969 Supreme Court argument, his lawyer reported 16 months in jail. The 1970 vacatur did not end the prosecution: Florida reconvicted him, and the conviction was upheld in 1972. APSP history reports renewed imprisonment on the mural charge in May 1973 and release within two months; the exact day of that release is unverified. Cutting reports that on October 29, 1973, Judge David Seth Walker reduced the sentence to 18 months already served. The recorded release date of October 29, 1973 is an editorial assumption based on that sentence reduction; it is not independently verified as the day he left prison. Yeshitela later recalled two and a half years in prison for the mural. No continuous custody interval or reconciled final duration is established.

editorial_notes: Adds one historical case summarizing the mural prosecutions and interrupted custody; does not edit any biography, website, photo, profile status, or existing modern case.

Keep numeric custody totals unset. The sources give an interim 16 months, 18 months recognized at sentence reduction, and a later two-and-a-half-year recollection. These may refer to different accounting of interrupted custody; do not force a reconciliation.
